“Hello, hello, Devorah Leah!” Freida said as she stepped inside. Reb Kaddish smiled kindly.

Freida patted her niece’s shoulder. “You look thin. Too thin, my dear.

A drawn look came over Devorah Leah’s face. She shrugged as she responded, “These days, he often sleeps there.”

Freida’s jaw dropped. “That’s no place for a growing boy to sleep! But, I’m getting ahead of myself. Devorah Leah, if I can trouble you, where can we sit?”

LAST TIME: When Baruch and Devorah are young teenagers, Rochel passes away. Within the year, Reb Shneur Zalman passes away, too, leaving his children doubly orphaned. Soon after the second shiva, a fancy carriage arrives at Devorah Leah and Baruch’s home. A New Home

Devorah Leah cleared her throat. “I deeply appreciate that you want

to take us in. But, I have one request. If it’s alright. I’d like to support myself, just like I do now.”

her basket in the corner. “Mamme taught me when I was young. And lately, I’ve taken other people’s sewing in as well, for money. Baruch Hashem, we have enough.”

Reb Kaddish nodded. “A young girl like you, Devorah Leah, shouldn’t have to worry about putting bread on the table. And taking care of you won’t be a burden in the slightest for your Aunt Freida and I. On the contrary … it will be special.”

Freida drew a handkerchief from her pocket, and dabbed at her eyes. “Uncle Kaddish and I would love to care for you and Baruch like the children we never had. We want to make sure that you have everything you need. Proper beds, nutritious food, fresh clothing. And absolutely no worries of working or supporting yourselves.”

There was a short silence. Devorah Leah shifted in her seat.

Then Freida sighed. “You’re like your father was, no? So unyielding. He was that way since he was a boy.”

it … that would be wonderful,” answered Devorah Leah. She smiled nervously. “The truth is … it gets lonely here, especially

on the long nights when Baruch isn’t home. It would be so nice to be in a house with others. But I need some time. A few days … until after Shabbos. I need time to gather my things and discuss all this with Baruch.”

Like I said, we’ll be back. See you next week! And have a wonderful day! We love you very much.”
